findings.message: <video id="base"> has src but no data-start. HyperFrames cannot own playback for untimed media, so preview and render behavior can diverge.
findings.fixHint: This <video> sits inside the timed <div id="footage"> (data-start="0"), and the wrapper's data-start would then clash. Move the <video> out as a direct child of the stage and give it that wrapper's data-start="0" and data-duration="21.700".

findings.message: Composition uses GSAP but no GSAP script is loaded. The animation will not run.
<div id="footage"> is a timeline element that contains nested <div id="cam">. The timeline shows one row per top-level element, and the root composition is built only from sub-compositions.
findings.fixHint: Move <div id="footage"> and its contents into a sub-composition file and mount it with data-composition-src.

findings.message: GSAP tween on "#hook-kicker" uses motion that snaps to integer device pixels: letterSpacing. Layout and text-reflow properties snap during browser layout; roundProps rounds the tween value. Slow motion or an ease-out tail then stutters under the seek-by-frame capture engine. Animate transforms (x/y/scale/opacity) instead.
findings.fixHint: do not animate letterSpacing (they reflow text and snap glyph positions): for letterSpacing, split the text into per-character elements and animate each glyph's x (the spread), since uniform scale is NOT equivalent, or hold the final value statically. Transforms interpolate sub-pixel and stay smooth at any speed.

findings.message: Font family used without @font-face declaration: space grotesk. These are not in the auto-resolved font list, so the renderer cannot supply them automatically. Text will fall back to a generic font, producing incorrect typography in the video.
findings.fixHint: Add @font-face { font-family: '...'; src: url('capture/assets/fonts/...woff2'); } for each font family, pointing to the captured .woff2 files. For an OS-bundled system font (e.g. Hiragino Sans, Microsoft YaHei) that has no downloadable file, use src: local('Exact Font Name') instead. The declaration alone satisfies this check without needing a font file.
